newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK COUPON BONDS GAIN MORE GROUND AFTER SANTER.
newsitem.headline: GREEK COUPON BONDS GAIN MORE GROUND AFTER SANTER.

text.p: Greek fixed coupon bonds were keeping their positive slant intact and registered fresh gains after EU commission president Jacques Santer said Greece could fulfil EMU criteria at the end of 1998, bond dealers said.
Ecu/drachma was trading narrowly around 309.70 and depos and forex forwards were holding morning levels, traders said.

"Bonds, especially three-year coupon bonds, have gained another 25 to 40 basis points in terms of price," said a bond trader at a private bank. "We have seen strong buying interest from abroad after Santer's statement."
The president of the EU commission, Jacques Santer, said the Greek economy had made considerable progress and could meet the convergence criteria for EMU entry at the end of 1998.
Santer who is visiting Athens to participate in the celebrations for Europe Day spoke to reporters after meeting with Prime Minister Costas Simitis.
The mark was quoted at 159.07/12 from Friday's 159.260 fix, the dollar at 271.21/31 drachmas from 270.710 and the ecu at 309.73/83 from 309.780 drachmas.
